content: Friends hold a mirror up to each other; through the other, each sees his own soul.
author: Aristotle
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Genuine love is not a transaction where you keep score of who gave what; it is a state of being where you extend warmth and goodwill without needing to control the other person.

In Aristotle's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. The biggest barrier to deep connection is never external; it is our own fear of rejection. We build armor around our hearts to avoid pain, but that same armor ends up locking out the warmth and intimacy we crave.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
